title: Simplifi Alternatives 2026: Pricing and Features Compared
h1: Simplifi Alternatives 2026: Pricing and Features Compared
metaDescription: Compare Simplifi alternatives: Monarch, YNAB, Copilot Money, PocketGuard, EveryDollar and Tiller, with published pricing and budgeting methods.
intro:
Monarch, YNAB (You Need A Budget), Copilot Money, PocketGuard, EveryDollar and Tiller are the six budgeting apps covered. Their published prices run from a free tier on EveryDollar to $14.99 a month on Monarch Core or YNAB monthly, and they differ in budgeting method, platform support and trial terms. At The Modern Wallet, we lay out the published plan prices and feature limits so the dollar difference between subscriptions is visible before you sign up.

[Simplifi](https://www.simplifimoney.com) is a cloud-based budgeting app for web and mobile made by Quicken. Simplifi shows $3.99 per month alongside $6.99, labeled as billed annually, as a first-year offer for new memberships ordered directly by December 8, 2026 at 12:00 AM Pacific Standard Time (PST). The alternatives price differently: EveryDollar offers a free manual tier, PocketGuard adds a one-time lifetime payment option, and Tiller connects to private spreadsheets.

For a broader look at personal finance tools, see our [best budgeting apps roundup](/roundup/best-budgeting-apps/) and our [best net worth tracker roundup](/roundup/best-net-worth-tracker/). If you are evaluating desktop software with local file storage, our [Quicken alternatives](/alternatives/quicken/) guide covers Quicken Classic desktop. To model category allocations, test our [zero-based budget calculator](/budget/zero-based-budget-calculator/) and read our [guide to making a budget](/guides/how-to-make-a-budget/). You can also browse our wider [comparison hub](/compare/).

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Simplifi Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Start with the budgeting method. Simplifi uses a Spending Plan where bills, subscriptions and savings goals come out first, leaving remaining money available to spend or save. Simplifi notes that this structure works with zero-based budgeting, envelope budgeting, and 50-30-20 plans. In contrast, YNAB and EveryDollar center on giving every dollar a job. PocketGuard builds its system around rollover budgeting, transaction rules and category budgets. Tiller syncs bank data into private Google Sheets spreadsheets.

Next, examine the pricing structure and renewal terms. EveryDollar publishes a free tier that allows manual transaction entry for as long as you want. Paid annual plans among the alternatives range from $74.99 per year for PocketGuard Plus and $79.99 per year for EveryDollar Premium, to $99 per year for Tiller, $99.99 for Monarch Core, and $109 for YNAB and Copilot Money. PocketGuard also sells a lifetime license for a single $149.99 payment. On monthly schedules, YNAB and Monarch Core cost $14.99, PocketGuard costs $12.99, and EveryDollar Premium costs $17.99. Simplifi displays $3.99 per month alongside $6.99 labeled as billed annually for new members ordering before December 8, 2026, and its footnote states that subscriptions renew at then-current rates.

Trial terms also separate these providers. YNAB provides a 34-day free trial with no payment card required when registering directly on its site. Tiller offers a 30-day trial where the card is not charged until the period ends, paired with a second 30-day refund window. Monarch's first week is free, and it lists a money-back guarantee. EveryDollar offers a 14-day trial for Premium. PocketGuard requires a payment card upfront for its 7-day trial, and Copilot Money lists no trial duration on its pricing page.

Consider platform availability and sharing limits before deciding. Copilot Money supports iPhone, iPad, Mac and Web, but lists no Android app. PocketGuard supports iPhone, Android and web. Simplifi allows sharing with one other person through spaces and sharing. YNAB allows sharing with a group of up to six people under a single subscription. Monarch has Core and Plus plans with no ads. Geographic boundaries matter as well: Quicken notes that Simplifi is not designed to function outside the US and Canada. PocketGuard publishes bank connectivity across the US, Canada and the United Kingdom (UK).

Check these four items when comparing options:

- Does the budgeting system require manual entry or automatic bank connection?
- What is the regular annual renewal rate after any first-year promotional offer?
- How many people need access to the budget, and does sharing cost extra?
- Does the service work on your operating system and within your country?

alternatives.heading: Monarch Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Monarch is a subscription personal finance application with two plan tiers: Core and Plus. Core costs $99.99 per year or $14.99 per month. Plus costs $199.99 per year and adds forecasting tools, tracking for multiple income sources like a small business, and deeper investment features. Monarch's first week is free. Monarch displays a promotional banner offering 30% off Core for one year with code WELCOME, noting that terms apply and the code may expire. Subscriptions can be canceled at any time, backed by a money-back guarantee. Monarch recommends signing up on the web rather than through mobile app stores, displays no ads, and states that it never sells customer financial data.

Worked cost example: Paying for Monarch Core month to month at $14.99 costs 12 x $14.99 = $179.88 over twelve months. The annual Core plan costs $99.99 per year, saving $79.89 compared to monthly billing before any promotional discount. Monarch Plus at $199.99 per year costs $100.00 more per year than Core on annual billing. Simplifi's pricing page lists $3.99 per month alongside $6.99 billed annually for the first year, but states that the final annual price may differ from the monthly discounted price multiplied by 12 months, so a direct 12-month comparison against Simplifi cannot be computed from that page.

Monarch fits people who want an ad-free budgeting dashboard with the option to track multiple revenue sources like a small business on Plus. Versus Simplifi, Monarch publishes clear standard renewal rates of $99.99 for Core and $199.99 for Plus. Simplifi provides free one-on-one setup help from Quicken experts and includes a Health Score checking 9 financial areas, features not listed on Monarch's pricing page.

alternatives.heading: YNAB Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
YNAB sells a personal budgeting subscription based on its proprietary method, which prompts users to decide what each dollar is for. The annual plan costs $109 per year, which equates to $9.08 per month and represents what YNAB advertises as a $70 savings over paying monthly. The monthly plan costs $14.99 per month, plus applicable sales tax, with all figures in US dollars. YNAB provides a 34-day free trial that requires no credit card when signing up directly on its website, though app stores may require payment details. College students can obtain a free 365-day trial. A single YNAB subscription can be shared with a group of up to six people.

Features include account connection, goal targets, real-time syncing across devices, and debt payoff tools with an integrated loan calculator. YNAB does not support multiple currencies together in one spending plan.

Worked cost example: Billed monthly at $14.99 per month, YNAB costs 12 x $14.99 = $179.88 over a full year. The annual plan costs $109, which is $70.88 cheaper than twelve monthly payments, matching YNAB's advertised $70 savings after rounding. Compared with Monarch Core's $99.99 annual rate, YNAB costs $9.01 more per year.

YNAB fits budgeters who want an active method where they assign every dollar a job and share access with up to six people. Versus Simplifi, YNAB includes sharing for six people, whereas Simplifi limits sharing to one other person through spaces and sharing. Simplifi includes 12-month projected cash flow, automated watchlist tracking and retirement planning tools, while YNAB lists targets and debt tools instead.

alternatives.heading: Copilot Money Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Copilot Money offers a personal finance application built for Apple platforms and the web. Copilot Money features one plan with no tiers. Its pricing page shows an annual rate of $109 billed yearly, displayed as $9 per month under a limited-time offer marked down from its regular $119 price. Copilot Money connects to more than 16,000 banks and provides support from real humans alongside a built-in money assistant. The software runs on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Web. The pricing page notes that partner invitations are listed as coming this fall.

Worked cost example: At $9 per month, twelve months of Copilot Money equals $108, which is $1 less than the $109 billed yearly. Against its standard $119 yearly price, the $109 limited-time rate saves $10.00. Copilot Money's $109 annual rate matches YNAB's $109 annual fee and sits $9.01 above Monarch Core's $99.99 annual plan.

Copilot Money fits individuals using Apple devices who want bank connectivity and a money assistant under a single flat rate. Versus Simplifi, Copilot Money lists no Android app, while Simplifi runs on web and mobile platforms across operating systems. Simplifi also connects to over 14,000 institutions, includes spaces and sharing for two people today, and provides free one-on-one setup help from Quicken experts.

alternatives.heading: PocketGuard Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
PocketGuard offers personal budgeting through its PocketGuard Plus tier across web, iPhone and Android platforms. PocketGuard Plus publishes three payment options: Yearly at $74.99 billed annually (equating to $6.25 per month, advertised with a Save $81/year callout), Monthly at $12.99 per month (totaling $155.88 per year), and Lifetime access for a single payment of $149.99. All plans include a 7-day free trial that requires entering a payment method upfront, and the subscription starts automatically when the trial finishes. PocketGuard displays no ads and states that it does not sell personal financial data.

Features include unlimited bank account connections across the US, Canada and the UK, unlimited category budgets, rollover budgeting, subscription tracking, cash accounts, transaction rules, debt payoff planning, transaction import and export, priority human customer support and artificial intelligence (AI) chat.

Worked cost example: Paying $12.99 monthly totals 12 x $12.99 = $155.88 over twelve months, while the yearly rate is $74.99, establishing an annual difference of $80.89. The Lifetime plan costs $149.99 once. Two years of the yearly plan equal 2 x $74.99 = $149.98. The lifetime option costs less than ongoing yearly payments after just over two years of use. At $74.99 per year, PocketGuard Plus is $25.00 cheaper annually than Monarch Core ($99.99) and $34.01 cheaper than YNAB ($109).

PocketGuard fits people who want rollover category budgeting, bank sync across the US, Canada and the UK, and the ability to eliminate recurring subscription fees with a lifetime license. Versus Simplifi, PocketGuard requires a payment method to begin its 7-day trial. Simplifi provides cash flow projections 12 months ahead and sharing with one other person through spaces and sharing.

alternatives.heading: EveryDollar Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
EveryDollar is a zero-based budgeting application created by Ramsey Solutions that focuses on giving every dollar a job. EveryDollar provides a free version that users can keep as long as they want. The free plan includes a monthly budget, unlimited budget categories, manual transaction entry, sinking funds, split transactions, bill due dates and live customer support. EveryDollar Premium begins with a 14-day free trial and costs $79.99 billed annually (shown as $6.67 per month), or $17.99 per month on a monthly billing schedule.

EveryDollar Premium adds automated bank connections that stream transactions in via Mastercard Connect and Plaid, custom reports, comma-separated values (CSV) transaction export, financial roadmap goals, live question-and-answer sessions with financial coaches, and net worth projection modeling.

Worked cost example: Twelve months of EveryDollar Premium on monthly billing costs 12 x $17.99 = $215.88. The annual subscription costs $79.99 per year, creating an annual savings of $135.89 compared to monthly payments. The free tier costs $0, saving $79.99 per year compared to Premium and $99.99 compared to Monarch Core.

EveryDollar fits people who want zero-based budgeting and either prefer a $0 manual entry plan or want automated bank feeds with coaching access. Versus Simplifi, EveryDollar publishes a permanent free tier, whereas Simplifi requires a paid subscription. However, EveryDollar Premium costs $17.99 month to month, which is higher than the monthly rates of Monarch ($14.99), YNAB ($14.99) and PocketGuard ($12.99). Simplifi also connects to over 14,000 institutions and includes projected cash flow looking 12 months ahead.

alternatives.heading: Tiller Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Tiller is a financial tracking service that syncs account balances and daily transactions directly into private spreadsheets that you own. Tiller works inside Google Sheets and costs $99 per year plus applicable sales tax. Tiller provides a 30-day free trial where payment cards are not charged until the trial concludes, followed by a 30-day money-back guarantee, allowing up to 60 days of risk-free evaluation. Users sign up using a Microsoft or Google account.

Tiller connects to financial institutions to pull updated financial data automatically each day. Tiller supports tracking solo business income and expenses alongside household budgets. Users can also connect an external artificial intelligence tool directly to their personal spreadsheets for custom analysis.

Worked cost example: At $99 per year, Tiller works out to an average monthly cost of $8.25 per month ($99 divided by 12). Over three years, Tiller totals $297.00. Monarch Core totals $299.97 over three years ($99.99 x 3), and YNAB totals $327.00 ($109 x 3).

Tiller fits spreadsheet enthusiasts and solo business owners who want automated transaction feeds inside Google Sheets. Versus Simplifi, Tiller works in Google Sheets. Simplifi provides dedicated mobile and web applications, automated spending categorization, a 9-point Health Score, and one-on-one setup help from Quicken experts.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
This comparison focuses strictly on consumer personal budgeting and cash flow applications. It is not suitable for several groups of readers.

- Small businesses requiring full double-entry accounting, balance sheets, inventory tracking and accounts payable management. Dedicated accounting software covers those needs.
- People living outside the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, because Quicken says Simplifi is not designed to function outside the US and Canada, and PocketGuard lists connectivity in the US, Canada and UK only.
- Anyone who refuses to connect financial accounts or manually log transactions. Each app on this page works from account or transaction data.
- Individuals seeking personalized legal or investment advice. This page lists published prices and gives no advice.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on Simplifi Alternatives
alternatives.body:
The comparisons on this page reflect published pricing and product features as of November 23, 2026. Several updates would change how these budgeting tools compare.

- Simplifi publishing a single, fixed renewal price rather than listing $3.99 per month alongside $6.99 billed annually with variable renewal disclaimers.
- Simplifi officially releasing its investment performance tools, which are currently marked coming soon for time-weighted and money-weighted returns.
- Monarch adjusting its $99.99 Core or $199.99 Plus annual price points, or ending its 30% WELCOME promotional discount.
- YNAB altering its $109 annual list price, changing its 34-day credit-card-free trial, or modifying its six-person sharing rule.
- Copilot Money launching its partner invitation feature, releasing an Android app, or ending its $109 promotional rate against its standard $119 fee.
- PocketGuard removing its $149.99 lifetime payment option or altering its $74.99 annual price.
- EveryDollar modifying the features available on its permanent free tier or changing its $79.99 annual Premium subscription.
- Tiller introducing a month-to-month payment option or raising its $99 annual fee.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Simplifi Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Simplifi remains the better fit for individuals and households who want automated spending plans, multi-account aggregation and long-term cash flow forecasting in one cloud application. Simplifi connects to over 14,000 financial institutions, categorizing transactions automatically and surfacing recurring bills and subscriptions. Its Spending Plan automatically reserves money for bills, subscriptions and savings goals before displaying what is left to spend, supporting zero-based budgeting, envelope budgeting and 50-30-20 models.

Simplifi also provides Projected Cash Flow modeling that charts account balances up to 12 months into the future, helping users plan around upcoming obligations. Net worth tracking, custom spending reports, customizable category Watchlists, and Savings Goals with required monthly contributions are all included. Simplifi incorporates Quicken AI to answer questions based on your connected accounts and a Quicken Health Score that evaluates 9 financial areas. New subscribers receive free one-on-one setup help from Quicken experts, and accounts can be shared with one other person through spaces and sharing.

For customers who want Quicken's financial tracking on web and mobile without storing files locally on a computer as Quicken Classic requires, Simplifi delivers cloud access. Simplifi displays a first-year promotional price of $3.99 per month and $6.99 billed annually for new members ordering directly before December 8, 2026 at 12:00 AM Pacific Standard Time (PST), with automatic renewal at then-current rates.

verdict: EveryDollar provides a permanent $0 free plan for manual budgeting, while PocketGuard Plus offers the lowest annual paid price at $74.99 alongside a $149.99 lifetime option. Tiller automates feeds into Google Sheets for $99 per year, Monarch Core costs $99.99 per year with a Plus tier at $199.99, and YNAB and Copilot Money each charge $109 annually. Simplifi lists an introductory rate of $3.99 per month alongside $6.99 billed annually for new members, featuring 12-month projected cash flow and setup guidance from Quicken specialists. The next step for anyone weighing Simplifi alternatives is to open each provider's pricing page, confirm the current price and trial terms, and compare them with the table above.

faqs.question: Is Simplifi free?
faqs.answer: No. Simplifi is a paid subscription service. Its pricing page displays $3.99 per month alongside $6.99 labeled billed annually as a first-year promotional offer for new memberships ordered directly by December 8, 2026 at 12:00 AM Pacific Standard Time (PST). Subscriptions renew automatically at then-current rates.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest app like Simplifi?
faqs.answer: EveryDollar provides a free tier that costs $0 for as long as you want with manual transaction entry. Among paid annual subscriptions, PocketGuard Plus lists the lowest regular price at $74.99 per year ($6.25 per month), followed by EveryDollar Premium at $79.99 per year, Tiller at $99 per year, Monarch Core at $99.99 per year, and YNAB and Copilot Money at $109 per year.

faqs.question: Which Simplifi alternative uses zero-based budgeting?
faqs.answer: YNAB and EveryDollar are both built specifically around zero-based budgeting, where users assign every dollar a job. Simplifi notes that its Spending Plan can also accommodate zero-based budgeting, envelope budgeting and 50-30-20 approaches.

faqs.question: Which Simplifi alternative has a lifetime price?
faqs.answer: PocketGuard offers a Lifetime plan for a single one-time payment of $149.99, which provides permanent access to PocketGuard Plus without recurring subscription fees.

faqs.question: Does Simplifi work outside the US?
faqs.answer: Quicken states that its products, including Simplifi, are not designed to function outside the United States and Canada. PocketGuard lists bank connectivity in the US, Canada and the United Kingdom.
